public_rationale: The New Yorker questioned AI profitability and investor returns on October 27, 2025 [e1]. Portfolio manager Henry Neville questioned AI monetization and investment returns on October 29, 2025 [e2]. These show public economic doubts beyond Marcus during the October 26–November 2 target window [e1, e2]. A Reuters report available on October 28 also quoted investor Eric Schiffer rejecting the bubble characterization; that differing view does not negate the documented concerns [e3, e1, e2].
limitations: The evidence does not measure population-wide opinion, an increase in skepticism, or when skepticism began.
Expressions of concern do not establish that the industry is economically unsustainable or will fail [e1, e2].
Neville's commentary does not establish Man Group's collective position [e2].
The WSJ article and the claimed DeSantis amplification were not independently verified in the packet.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As of November 2025, people are starting to recognize that the generative AI industry lacks solid economic footing.

statement.excerpt: People are starting to look down.

from_speaker: People are starting to look down.
our_interpretation: The ordinary contextual reading is that doubts about generative AI's economic sustainability were becoming visible beyond Marcus's own commentary.
Look down means publicly question the economic footing of the boom. It does not require proof that the industry is unsustainable or agreement among most people.
Use the week ending on the post date, October 26 through November 2, for the recent public discussion described by the surrounding references.
Mainstream coverage and identifiable financial-market commentary are observable evidence of wider recognition. Marcus supplies no numerical threshold or measured growth rate.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous mainstream coverage and public commentary by financial-market participants explicitly question generative AI's profitability, investment returns or economic sustainability.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable contemporaneous evidence establishes that the supposed wider recognition was misrepresented and that the cited discussion did not express economic doubts. Optimistic voices alone do not contradict the existence of concern.
